findings.evidence: "the IT asset group tracks the stipend budget each quarter"
findings.fix: State one authoritative owner for stipend budget tracking and remove or reconcile the IT asset group's role with the finance/benefits team responsibilities described later.
findings.violation: This assigns stipend-budget ownership to the "IT asset group," which conflicts with later sections that attribute payout/financial responsibility to "the benefits team" (Program Coordination) and "the finance office" (Reimbursement Amounts, Review Responsibility), leaving the actual owner unclear.

findings.evidence: "If the position counts as full-time, the stipend can apply... Only once every condition above is met does the home-office equipment stipend become available"
findings.fix: Rewrite as one conjunctive sentence, e.g., "The stipend applies only when the position is full-time, the employee has completed 90 days of continuous service, and the request arrives before the benefit year ends."
findings.violation: Each conditional sentence is phrased as if that condition alone makes the stipend applicable, but the closing sentence requires all three conditions together, creating an internal contradiction between OR-style phrasing and an AND requirement.

findings.evidence: "If the position counts as full-time, the stipend can apply."
findings.fix: Define "full-time" with a concrete threshold, e.g., "regularly scheduled for at least 30 hours per week."
findings.violation: "Full-time" is never defined (no hours/week or FTE threshold given), so eligibility cannot be determined objectively.

findings.evidence: "If the request arrives before the benefit year ends, the stipend can apply."
findings.fix: Add an explicit definition of "benefit year" (e.g., calendar year, fiscal year, or anniversary of hire date).
findings.violation: "Benefit year" is used repeatedly as a load-bearing term (eligibility deadline, $500 cap) but its start/end dates are never defined anywhere in the document.

findings.evidence: "the backup reviewer who covers for absences was not told that the request needs sign-off before the portal releases the confirmation email"
findings.fix: Remove the anecdote or replace it with a general rule, e.g., "If the primary manager is unavailable, the designated backup reviewer is notified in advance and must approve before the confirmation email is sent."
findings.violation: This is a specific narrative about a process failure, not a general policy rule, and it doesn't tell the reader what to do or expect - it reads as an incident description embedded in policy text.

findings.evidence: "The request is reviewed within two business days."
findings.fix: Reconcile the two sections - note exceptions to the SLA for reviewer unavailability, or fix the backup-reviewer notification process so the two-day claim holds.
findings.violation: This fixed SLA contradicts the preceding "How to Apply" section, which describes an indefinite delay caused by an untrained backup reviewer.

findings.evidence: "The manager approves items pursuant to internal discretion, notwithstanding the standard review checklist."
findings.fix: Rewrite in plain language, e.g., "The manager approves items using the standard review checklist; any exception requires documented justification."
findings.violation: The legalistic phrasing is inconsistent with the plain-language tone used elsewhere, and its meaning is ambiguous/contradictory - it's unclear whether discretion overrides or supplements the checklist, which conflicts with Approval Timeline's statement that "the manager confirms the equipment category matches the approved list."

findings.evidence: "the deposit happens in order to offset costs the employee already paid at this point in time"
findings.fix: Simplify to "The deposit reimburses costs the employee already paid."
findings.violation: The phrase "at this point in time" is redundant filler that adds no information beyond "already paid," making the sentence unnecessarily wordy.

findings.evidence: three differing actors/timelines for the same payout step
findings.fix: Pick one authoritative statement of who disburses funds and on what schedule, and delete the conflicting statements in the other sections.
findings.location: Reimbursement Amounts ("The finance office deposits the amount within one pay cycle"), compared with Program Coordination ("the team schedules the reimbursement for the next pay cycle") and Terminology Notes ("Payroll releases the stipend item amount after that monthly review")
findings.violation: Three sections attribute the disbursement action to three different parties (finance office, benefits team, payroll) with three different schedules (one pay cycle, next pay cycle, after monthly review), contradicting each other.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in third person, e.g., "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition; the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: This sentence switches to second-person "you/we" voice, breaking from the third-person voice ("the employee," "the manager") used everywhere else in the document.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Replace "Similarly" with "Additionally," or state the rule as its own sentence without a connector.
findings.violation: "Similarly" implies parallelism with the prior sentence about photo checks, but the one-device-per-category rule is unrelated, making the transition logically wrong.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the stipend item against the request log each month."
findings.fix: Define "stipend item" on first use or replace it with an already-defined term (e.g., "the approved equipment"), and convert the passage to third person.
findings.violation: "Stipend item" is never defined - it's unclear whether it refers to the purchased equipment, the dollar amount, or the request itself - and the section also reverts to second-person voice inconsistent with the rest of the document.

findings.evidence: "Also, you submit the request in the portal. You track its status there until the payment clears."
findings.fix: Delete this sentence, or move any genuinely new detail (status tracking) into "How to Apply" and remove the repeat here.
findings.violation: This duplicates information already stated in "How to Apply," adding redundancy without new content.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and uploading the receipt."
findings.fix: Remove this section as redundant, or rewrite it to match the full ordered process described in "How to Apply" and "Approval Timeline."
findings.violation: This contradicts "How to Apply," which states the process begins with starting the request in the benefits portal, and it omits manager review and other steps described elsewhere, making it an incomplete, inconsistent restatement of the process.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team publishes the reimbursement log after every open enrollment period."
findings.fix: Merge the two overview sections into one and state a single, consistent publisher and publication schedule.
findings.violation: This directly contradicts "Program Overview" at the top of the document, which states "The people operations office publishes the reimbursement log each quarter" - different publisher and different frequency for the same document.

findings.evidence: "Staff can request a printed copy from the benefits team at any time."
findings.fix: Delete the duplicate "Overview" section, keeping only "Program Overview."
findings.violation: This is a verbatim duplicate of a sentence already in "Program Overview," making the entire section redundant.

findings.evidence: "The team then routes the request to the correct approver based on department."
findings.fix: Clarify whether department-based routing and manager approval are the same step, and consolidate the full approval chain into one section.
findings.violation: This introduces department-based routing to "the correct approver," which is never reconciled with "Approval Timeline," where the only approver mentioned is "the manager" - it's unclear if these are the same step or an additional layer.

findings.evidence: "The finance office also flags any request that repeats within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Define what constitutes a "repeat" request, e.g., "a second request from the same employee within the same quarter."
findings.violation: "Repeats" is undefined - it's unclear whether it means the same employee submitting a second request, the same equipment category, or something else, making the rule unenforceable as written.

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out."
findings.fix: Consolidate all approval steps (manager review, department routing, finance threshold review) into the "Approval Timeline" section.
findings.violation: This adds an additional approval gate (finance review for amounts over $200) that is never mentioned in "Approval Timeline," which only describes a manager review within two business days, so the full approval process is inconsistently documented across sections.

findings.evidence: "The benefits team publishes the vendor list each quarter. Every entry carries a date stamp so the record stays easy to audit."
findings.fix: Rename the section to match its content (e.g., "Vendor List") or add actual instructions for how employees can ask questions or receive updates.
findings.violation: The section is titled "Questions and Updates" but contains no contact information or guidance for asking questions - its content doesn't match its heading, and the document ends without ever explaining how employees can ask a question.
